newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 22.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government has announced the creation of a powerful new Employment Committee - which will include the Government's senior economic Ministers - aimed at driving the Government's labour-market policies and helping to address the growing political focus on unemployment. Page 1.

Under a timetable unveiled by Communications Minister Richard Alston, the plan to shut down Telstra's A$1.75 billion Mobilenet analog phone network by the year 2000 will force Australia's 2.5 million analog users to scrap their mobile phones. An average o 3,300 users will have to surrender their phones each working-day as part of the three-year digital mobile upgrade plan. Page 1.

High Court judge Justice Michael Kirby has called for the development of an "alternative theory of the judicial function" which would be aimed at preventing excesses in judicial creativity. Kirby said the new theory was needed, in order to curb the "uncontrolled, idiosyncratic opinions of unelected judges". Page 5.

The Federal Opposition has come under pressure within its own ranks to re-think its own image following the convincing loss in the weekend's Lindsay by-election. However, Opposition Leader Kim Beazley remains firm, claiming Labor will not be forced to change strategy as the party continues to oppose major polices of the Federal Government. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Responding to widespread fears of a worsening outlook for jobseekers, Prime Minister John Howard last night moved to capitalise on his Government's resounding success in the Lindsay by-election by shifting the focus of its economic policies to jobs as a way of gaining support from the "battlers". Page 1.

Following the results of a reading comprehension survey commissioned by the Howard Government in June, which showed one in three Year 9 students do not have basic literacy skills, Minister for Schools, Vocational Education and Training David Kemp last night called for tough new school accountability measures to stem the decline in student literacy levels. Page 1.

Speaking before the United Nations General Assembly was due to vote this morning on whether to grant Australia a two-year seat on the UN Security Council, Australia's ambassador to the UN, Richard Butler, said Australia appears to have secured enough intenational support to win the bid. Page 1.

Five disgruntled St Luke's parishioners and their former minister, the Reverend David Greentree, have taken the extraordinary step of attempting to impeach the Anglican Primate of Australia, Archbishop Keith Rayner, who is also the Archbishop of Melbourne following a five-year dispute which has divided the congregation. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

An internal Sydney Water draft report has revealed that Sydney-siders have been exposed on at least two occasions to a very high risk of infection from Cryptosporidium - a potentially fatal gut parasite - in their tap water in recent years, with levels in the water distribution system at times high enough to cause a gastro-intestinal disease epidemic. Page 1.

Following France's decision to stop nuclear testing and sign the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, the Federal Government moved yesterday to lift its ban on new uranium contracts - a move that clears the way for Australia to gain an increased share of Frances uranium market for nuclear electric power generation. Page 1.

After already appearing before the Police Royal Commission in December 1994, former New South Wales Police Commissioner Tony Lauer has been subpoenaed to give evidence again, for hearings believed to be commencing next week. Page 1.

Releasing details of a national survey of literacy skills over the past 20 years, which has revealed schools have failed to improve standards, Federal Schools Minister David Kemp warned that standards will not improve until the 'cult of secrecy' was broke and parents were given more information on school performance. Page 1.
THE AGE

Supreme Court Judge Justice Philip Cummins said yesterday Victoria's child protection system had failed 20-month-old Dillion Matthew Palfrey, who was killed when violently shaken by his intellectually impaired mother Rosa Maria Richards, 31, who has been entenced to seven years jail. Page A1.

A 20-year study of the abilities of 28,000 14-year-old students has found almost one third have inadequate basic literacy skills, prompting Federal Schools Minister David Kemp to say it showed there was a direct link between poor literacy levels, school drop-out rates and youth unemployment. Page A1.

The Victorian Government solicitor, Ronald Beazley, has described moves by mining giant, BHP, appealing a criminal case directly to State Attorney-General Jan Wade as "unusual". In January this year, BHP sent a two-volume submission to Wade, which argued hy the company should not be prosecuted for criminal contempt of court. Page A1.

The Department of Human Services' internal inquiry into the closure of the Dillion Palfrey case - where a baby died in the care of his mother and her de facto husband - slammed the office dealing with the case, claiming the decision was premature and poory planned. The inquiry also found that 63 per cent of the Department's staff involved in the case had less than 12 month's experience by March 1995, when baby Dillion died. Page A1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
